narrative: Third round of bp35 L9 exploration in this session, following round 14's lead to try interacting with objects other than the two start-room switches. Clicking directly on the pillar visible from the true-start view (color-15, originally at rows[13:18] cols[37:42]) does NOT kill the player (unlike walking into a pillar's eye end) -- instead it GROWS the pillar into a larger cross/plus-shaped cluster: the original block plus two new pillar blocks appearing to its left and right (rows[13:17] cols[31:36] and cols[43:48]) and one appearing above it (rows[7:11] cols[37:42]), for a total pillar cell count of 84 (up from the original 21). A second click at the same display coordinates produced no further change (same 84-cell count), suggesting either the growth is capped after one click or the second click landed on an already-grown, non-reactive part of the cluster. This is a genuinely new mechanic for this game not previously documented in the registry -- prior bp35 levels only described pillars as passive hazards (lethal at the eye end, inert elsewhere) and TOGGLE BLOCKS/E-doors as the growable/interactive objects. The state remained NOT_FINISHED throughout (not fatal to click or to have grown pillars nearby while not touching them). Not yet determined: whether the newly-grown pillar cells are hazardous (do they have their own eye ends?), whether this growth is useful as a platform/shield (per the established solidify-for-a-shelf pattern used elsewhere with toggle blocks), or whether it connects to reaching the goal, the 3rd switch, or the doors in any way. No new level banked; frontier stays at level 8.
novel_mechanics_found: PILLARS ARE CLICKABLE and GROW when clicked (color-15 cross/plus expansion, 21 cells -> 84 cells after one click), without harming the player. This is a previously-undocumented interaction for bp35 -- prior gotchas describe pillars only as passive lethal hazards. A second click at the same spot produced no further change.
